review.translation: [Then he drank|0] [some of|1] [the wine|2], [and he became drunk|3], [and he uncovered himself|4] [inside|5] [his tent|6].

analysis.evidence: מִן הַיַּיִן identifies what he drank as some of the wine. The next verb, וַיִּשְׁכָּר, describes the result, “and he became drunk.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ introduces a third-person masculine singular Qal wayyiqtol. The final ה of שָׁתָה drops out in this shortened form.

draft.change: Clarify that the Hebrew partitive sense includes a portion of a whole as well as members of a group. Add Genesis 9:21 as evidence for the use with a substance.
draft.definition: Introduces a group from which one or more members are taken or identified, or a whole of which a portion is taken.
draft.evidence: In Genesis 7:8–9 the animals come in pairs from among the groups named. In Genesis 9:21 מִן הַיַּיִן marks the unspecified portion of the wine that Noah drank.

analysis.evidence: In Genesis 9:21, וַיֵּשְׁתְּ מִן הַיַּיִן means “he drank some of the wine.” מִן introduces the wine as the whole from which Noah drank an unspecified amount.
analysis.morphology: Standalone Hebrew preposition with no prefix or pronominal suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּשְׁתְּ מִן־הַיַּיִן says that Noah drank some of the wine. The next verb, וַיִּשְׁכָּר, says that he became drunk, making the wine’s intoxicating effect explicit.
analysis.morphology: The definite article הַ doubles the initial י of יַיִן, a masculine singular noun in the absolute state.

analysis.evidence: וַיֵּשְׁתְּ מִן הַיַּיִן says that Noah drank some of the wine. וַיִּשְׁכָּר gives the result for that same subject: he became drunk.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ is prefixed to a Qal wayyiqtol verb in the third person masculine singular, with Noah as the subject.

analysis.evidence: Noah remains the subject after וַיִּשְׁכָּר (“and he became drunk”). The reflexive Hithpael describes him uncovering himself, and בְּתוֹךְ אָהֳלֹה places the action inside his tent.
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וַ precedes a third-person masculine singular Hithpael wayyiqtol. The final ה of the root drops out in this shortened form.

draft.change: Link the occurrence to תָּוֶךְ at word index 0 in twk. The current article already contains the published clarification for Genesis 9:21.
draft.definition: The interior of something that encloses. With בְּ, the expression means “inside” or “within.”
draft.evidence: Genesis 9:21 uses בְּתוֹךְ אָהֳלֹה for the location of Noah’s uncovering himself, inside his tent. The current תוכ article cites this occurrence under tavek-inside.

analysis.evidence: בְּתוֹךְ אָהֳלֹה tells where Noah uncovered himself. The tent supplies the enclosure, and בְּ locates the action within it.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ, “in,” prefixes תוֹךְ, the masculine singular construct of the common noun תָּוֶךְ. The following אָהֳלֹה, “his tent,” completes the construct.
analysis.sense: The interior of an enclosed place.

analysis.evidence: בְּתוֹךְ אָהֳלֹה means “inside his tent.” The phrase gives the place where Noah uncovered himself, and the suffix identifies Noah as the tent’s owner.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the construct state with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix, written ־ֹה.
